# Set-up

This markdown prepares the BAL inflammation dataset for analysis. The dataset was downloaded from the [Zenodod](https://zenodo.org/records/19364848). We selected batch 9 for this analysis as this batch contained 8 samples, each from different donors. Batch 3 was sequenced in two captures (each of which contains all samples), which are referred to as `C133_batch3_1` and `C133_batch3_`. Here, we only focus on `C133_batch3_1`.

The files downloaded are 

- raw feature_bc_matrix.h5 file (C133_batch3_1)

- processed SCE object for all of batch 3 (C133_batch3_1+C133_batch3_2) - the code for how this object was produced can be found [here](https://oshlacklab.com/paediatric-cf-inflammation-citeseq/01.3_preprocess_batch3.html). Note that the metadata for this object includes HTO and vireo results for doublet/singlet calls. We will need to filter out barcodes from the second capture. 

We will export a `cellranger` like output structure that contains both singlets and doublets.

## Load data

```{r}
# load raw counts
counts_raw <- Read10X_h5(here("data/BAL_inflammation_10x/C133_batch3_1/raw_feature_bc_matrix.h5"))$`Gene Expression`

#load count filtered SCE (provided by authors)
sce <- readRDS(here("data/BAL_inflammation_10x/C133_Neeland_batch3.preprocess.SCE.rds"))


#this wil contain both captures from batch 3 -> filter to only include 3_1
batch_3_1_cells <- sce[,sce$Capture == "C133_batch3_1"]

```


# Inspect genetic vs HTO demultiplexing

For both batches

```{r, fig.align='center', fig.height=6, fig.width=6}
p <- scater::plotColData(
  sce,
  "dmmHTO", 
  "GeneticDonor", 
  colour_by = "GeneticDonor", 
  other_fields = "Capture") +
  scale_x_discrete(guide = guide_axis(n.dodge = 2)) +
  guides(colour = "none")
p / (p + facet_grid(~Capture))
```

How many are considered doublets in both genetic as well as HTO (capture 3_1 only)

```{r}

batch_3_1_cells@colData %>% as.data.frame() %>% 
  filter(., dmmHTO == "Doublet" & GeneticDonor == "Doublet") %>% 
  nrow()

```


# Prepare metadata 

According to the original authors, the genetic demultiplexing was much more reliable and we therefore consider it the ground truth labels.

```{r}
#tidy up metadata a bit
meta_batch_3_1 <- batch_3_1_cells@colData %>% as.data.frame() %>% 
  select(., Barcode, GeneticDonor, dmmHTO) %>% 
  mutate(., doublet_class = case_when(!GeneticDonor %in% c("Unknown", "Doublet") ~ "singlet", #to match style
                                      GeneticDonor == "Doublet" ~ "doublet",
                                      GeneticDonor == "Unknown" ~ "remove")) 
```

```{r}
meta_batch_3_1$doublet_class %>% table()
```

What does that make the doublet rate (not considering remove section)

```{r}

table(meta_batch_3_1$doublet_class)["doublet"]/sum(table(meta_batch_3_1$doublet_class)["doublet"] + table(meta_batch_3_1$doublet_class)["singlet"])

```

About 20% doublet rate. 



# Prepare `cellranger` output

Make `cellranger` output files for barcodes that were detected as non-empty by the original authors (based on their SCE object).

## Make SCE object and add QC metrics

```{r}
#change rownames from metadata as they follow the old nomenclature that is no longer relevant
rownames(meta_batch_3_1) <- meta_batch_3_1$Barcode

export_sce <- SingleCellExperiment(assays = c("counts" = counts_raw[, meta_batch_3_1$Barcode]), 
                                   colData =meta_batch_3_1 %>% DataFrame())
  
#add QC metrics
is.mito <- grepl(pattern = "^MT", rownames(export_sce))
is.ribo <- grepl(pattern = "^RP[SL]", rownames(export_sce))
export_sce <- addPerCellQCMetrics(export_sce, subsets = list(mito = is.mito, ribo=is.ribo))

#clean up
new_meta <- export_sce@colData %>% as.data.frame() %>%
  dplyr::rename(.,nfeatures_raw = detected, ncount_raw = sum, subsets_mito_percent_raw = subsets_mito_percent, subsets_ribo_percent_raw=subsets_ribo_percent) %>%
  select(., -c("subsets_mito_sum", "subsets_mito_detected", "total", "subsets_ribo_sum", "subsets_ribo_detected", starts_with("altexps")))

export_sce@colData <- new_meta %>% DataFrame()
```

## Export 

Export in `cellranger` output format, including metadata.

```{r}
#export counts
output_dir <- here("output/data/BAL_inflammation_10x/BAL_inflammation_10x_cellranger/")
DropletUtils::write10xCounts(path = output_dir,
                             x = counts(export_sce),
                             version = "3",
                             overwrite = T)
#and export metadata
write_tsv(x= as.data.frame(export_sce@colData), file = paste0(output_dir, "metadata.tsv"),
          col_names = T)

```


# Prepare *empty droplets* `cellranger` output

Having an object that represent just the empty droplets is very useful when performing ambient RNA correction, so we'll export an empty droplets object in `cellranger` format as well. 


We'll use all the barcodes that were not considered non-empty (so empty) by the original authors. 

```{r}
#subset counts
empty_object <- counts_raw[, !(colnames(counts_raw) %in% export_sce$Barcode)]
```



```{r}
#export counts
output_dir <- here("output/data/BAL_inflammation_10x/BAL_inflammation_10x_emptyObject")
DropletUtils::write10xCounts(path = output_dir,
                             x = empty_object,
                             version = "3",
                             overwrite = T)
```
